reasoning: b-imperfect first person of iftakar: baftikir, the ordinary Ramallah 'I think'. inno is the Palestinian complementiser; the ellipsis is not romanized.
ma fii is the Palestinian 'there isn't'. heek 'like this' has ee, not ii, and the initial hamza of a7san is written as the bare vowel.
Form II with shadda on ث, initial hamza written as the vowel. In Ramallah this learned root is often said with s, assar fiyyi and ta'siir, since urban ث shifts to s in bookish words.
غ is gh and the shadda doubles ل: ghalla, the causative of ghili 'to be expensive'. Final alif maqsura is a.
Defective Form I, past jala, imperfect yijli; the verbal noun jaly is what Ramallah people call washing up. Final alif maqsura is a.
Fatha then a final cluster: shahm. Praise for a man who is chivalrous and steps up for others, slightly wider than plain 'noble'.
Shadda doubles ك and the stressed vowel is long ii: sikkiine, taa marbuta as e after ن.
Sukun on ج, taa marbuta as e after ب: wajbe. MSA in origin but ordinary in Ramallah speech, as in wajbet fTuur.
English loan with long oo then long aa in the stressed syllable. The scheme has no short e, so the unstressed vowels come out as a and i.
ث is t and the teen ending reduces to -na3sh in Palestinian: itna3sh, often tna3sh after a vowel. The given spelling already matches.
Defective Form I past rama, imperfect yirmi. In casual Ramallah speech zatt and kabb are also common for throwing something.
Palestinian imperfect prefix yi-, ح as 7, ظ as TH, realised in Ramallah as an emphatic z. The hyphen keeps TH and the following h from being read together.
The English gloss settles the unvowelled spelling: deen with ee is 'debt', against diin 'religion'. Plural dyuun.
The MSA diphthong aw becomes oo, and in a construct the taa marbuta is pronounced t, so I respell it مُوجِت. A weather-report phrase that Ramallah people do use in winter.

First member of the construct takes a pronounced t, so kurat; iid is the Palestinian 'hand', its initial hamza written as the vowel. In sports talk the MSA kurat il-yad is at least as common, hence low confidence.
The hamza is written after the article prefix, as in il-'usbuu3, and the shadda doubles و: il-'awwal.
European loan with three long vowels: miikaaniiki. Used for the car mechanic you take your car to.
Imperative khalli with shadda on ل plus the feminine object -ha. In fast speech 3ala allah runs together as 3a-llah.
Hollow verb with long aa: jaab, imperfect bijiib. The everyday Palestinian verb for bringing or fetching.
ع is 3, two fathas: 3ajal, plural 3jaal. In Ramallah it covers both the wheel and the tyre on it.
ذ merges with د in this core verb, so أخذ is respelled أَخَد. Initial hamza on alif is written as the bare vowel.
Initial hamza written as the vowel i, taa marbuta as e after و: ikhwe. Covers brothers and, loosely, siblings together.
ق is a glottal stop in this ordinary word, ط is T, ع is 3: 'aTii3. Used of sheep and goats.
raas 'head' with the first person -i, and 3een with ee. A warm Palestinian way of accepting a request outright.
Palestinian Form VI participle takes mit-, and ق is a glottal stop: mitfawwi'. It describes someone who excels, above all a top student, rather than 'superior' in the sense of better quality.
